rules.condition: register generation tool produces hardware output
rules.statement: The tool output is two Verilog files that can be instantiated by a peripheral following the Comportability Guidelines.

rules.condition: invoking the tool from the top project directory
rules.statement: The tool can be invoked from the top project directory to generate registers, e.g. for uart.
The name_reg2hw_t structure contains the signals driven from the register module to the rest of the hardware, including any required .q, .qe and .re signals.
The name_hw2reg_t structure contains the signals driven from the rest of the hardware to the register module, including any required .d and .de signals.

rules.condition: access targets an unmapped address fully representable with the internally used address bits
rules.statement: Accesses to unmapped addresses representable with the internal address bits typically return an error.

rules.condition: request to an unmapped address such as 0x88 with 8 internal address bits
rules.statement: A request to an address representable by the internal address bits but with no register mapped should return an error.

rules.condition: excess address bits stripped and resulting address is mapped
rules.statement: If the stripped address maps to a register, the request is forwarded to that register and no error is returned.

rules.condition: a_opcode has an illegal value
rules.statement: An error response is returned when TL-UL a_opcode has an illegal value.

rules.condition: TL-UL write of size smaller than the register size, e.g. 8b write to register wider than 8 bits
rules.statement: A write smaller than the register size returns an error.

rules.condition: write of size 8b or 16b to an address not 4B aligned
rules.statement: Sub-word writes that are not word-aligned return an error.

rules.condition: read smaller than full word (32b)
rules.statement: Reads smaller than a full word return the full register content and do not signal error.

rules.condition: sub-word read, e.g. one-byte read to address 0x3
rules.statement: Read response data is always in its byte channel, e.g. a byte read at 0x3 returns the full word with the correct byte in bits [31:24].

rules.condition: window access, based on declared validbits
rules.statement: The error rules above should be followed for windows based on the declared number of validbits, though this may be relaxed in some cases.

rules.condition: window terminates in a memory handling byte and halfword writes via masking
rules.statement: Errors need not be returned for unaligned sub-word writes.
Software write enable and write data have the highest priority in modifying register contents.

rules.condition: hwaccess allows hardware writes
rules.statement: Hardware can present updated values via de and d; when de is true the register content is updated with d.

rules.condition: software and hardware both request an update in the same cycle (de and we true)
rules.statement: The software-written value is used.

rules.condition: hwaccess is none
rules.statement: A hwaccess of none provides no hardware interface and may be used for registers only software can modify.

rules.condition: hwqe is true
rules.statement: qe is a registered version of the bus-side we, aligned with the change in q.

rules.condition: hwext register
rules.statement: No de input is required from peripheral hardware; only d is added to the struct bundle.

rules.condition: hwext register
rules.statement: qe timing is one cycle earlier than in the non-hwext model.

rules.condition: read-only registers
rules.statement: RO registers behave as RW registers with no wd and we inputs.

rules.condition: swaccess is ro, hwaccess is none or hro, and hwext is true
rules.statement: A software read returns a hardwired value equal to the register default value.

rules.condition: register type rc is read
rules.statement: When re indicates the register is being read, the contents are set to zero.
RC registers are not recommended, except for backwards compatibility.

rules.condition: register type RC
rules.statement: hwext must not be true for RC registers since re is not exported.

rules.condition: WO register with no storage needed, only write indication
rules.statement: hwext should be set to true so outside hardware handles the write event.

rules.condition: R0W1C, RW1S, RW1C, RW0C types
rules.statement: These types are implemented with special prim_subreg configuration so writing sets values in type-specific ways.
